title: yidam report envelope
description: The machine-readable report contract (RFC-0016 Phase 0). Every `yidam <command> --format json` emits this envelope with the command's own fields flattened alongside. Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields: adding one is not a breaking change, and `format_version` is bumped only when a consumer that understood the previous version would mis-read this one.

format_version.description: Contract major version. A consumer reading an unknown value MUST degrade loudly — disable verdict features and say why — and MUST NOT attempt to parse the rest.

yidam.description: Which yidam produced this. The handshake: a consumer is versioned independently of the binary a repository pins in .yidam.toml, so it must be able to detect skew.

commit.description: Short commit of the build, or the literal `unknown` when built without git. Never omitted, so 'not recorded' is distinguishable from 'absent'.

features.description: Cargo features compiled in. `reports` is the light default; others gate whole subcommands, so a consumer can tell 'this binary cannot do that' from 'that failed'.

root.description: Absolute path of the repository the report was computed over.

gate.description: `lint` only. The verdict — a consumer MUST NOT recompute it.

passed.description: Whether the run agrees with the committed baseline. Reflects the gate, not the process exit code: --warn-only exits 0 on a failing gate by design.

new_violations.description: Error-severity violations absent from the baseline. These fail CI.

baselined_violations.description: Error-severity violations the baseline already records. Inherited debt; these do not fail CI.

stale_baseline_entries.description: Baseline entries with no corresponding violation. These fail CI too — a baseline permitted to be wrong drifts.

checks.description: `lint` only. Every check that ran, including those that found nothing — a check that vanishes when it passes cannot be told from one that never ran.

id.description: Stable identifier; half of a violation's identity in the baseline.

severity.description: Only `error` gates, and only `error` is ever baselined.

node.description: The violation's identity, exactly as the baseline compares it. Unaffected by `span`.

in_baseline.description: Whether the committed baseline already records this violation. ONLY MEANINGFUL WHEN severity IS error — the baseline records error-severity violations and nothing else, so a warn or info violation is always false here. Read this together with `severity`, never alone.

span.description: Best-effort location. Output-only and never part of the violation's identity: a line number in the baseline's comparison would make it churn on every edit above a violation. Absent is a normal outcome — anchor at line 1.

passed.description: `graph-check`, `regen --check` and `index-verify`. The gate verdict. A consumer MUST NOT recompute it. On `due` it is true unless `--strict` was passed and a clock is due — being owed is not a failure, and this field is here so a consumer does not infer one.

failed.description: `doctor` only. Checks that are wrong now. The only ones that affect the exit code without `--strict`.

warned.description: `doctor` only. Checks that are actionable and a normal state to be in — a light build with no vector index, a pin from last season. They gate only under `--strict`, because a doctor that goes red on the normal state of a normal install is one people learn to pass `|| true`.

branch.description: `propose` only. The `propose/<head>` ref the proposals are written to. Reported whether or not the run wrote — on `--dry-run` it is where they would have gone.

head.description: `propose` only. The commit the proposals were drafted against and built on.

proposals.description: `propose` only. Each drafted commit, in the order it is committed. Three verbs only — `open`, `withdraw`, `close` — because nothing merges itself and nothing synthesizes; see RFC-0020.

verb.description: The epistemic verb the commit subject carries.

subject.description: The commit subject, in the closed vocabulary `lint --commits` checks.

check.description: The lint check whose finding this proposal answers.

node.description: Repo-relative path of the node or catalog entry the proposal is about.

detail.description: The finding's own words, which the commit body quotes. Carried so a consumer can check the carriage rule for itself rather than trusting that it held.

paths.description: Repo-relative paths the proposed commit changes.

skipped.description: `propose` only. Findings this run could not draft a proposal for, with the reason. Reported rather than swallowed: a finding silently not proposed about is the exact failure the command exists to remove.

reason.description: Why no proposal could be drafted — a `description:` that is not a block scalar, an entry with no closing frontmatter fence, or a message that would not carry its finding.

written.description: `propose` only. What reached the repository. Null on `--dry-run` and on a run with nothing to propose — the two states a consumer must not read as a write.

commits.description: Short shas, oldest first — the order `git log --reverse` prints them in.

withdraw_uncited_after.description: `propose` only. What the corpus licensed via `[propose] withdraw_uncited_after`. Null means no withdrawal may ever be drafted there, which is every corpus that has not said otherwise.

clocks.description: `due` only. The four clocks, each with the interval this corpus declared for it. A clock in state `undeclared` still reports what it measured: nobody has set it, which is not the same as its reading zero.

question.description: What the clock measures, in the form a person would ask it.

state.description: `due` is not a defect. A corpus with three expired sources is owed, not unhealthy — `doctor` is the report that answers whether anything is wrong. `undeclared` means this corpus set no interval, so the clock can never come due; `unmeasurable` means it set one and there is nothing to measure against, which is a gap in bookkeeping rather than a stale subject.

interval.description: The declaration that sets this clock's interval, as a reader would write it. Null when this corpus has not set one. The catalog clock reads `[catalog] ttl_days` and each entry's own `ttl_days:`; the other three read `[due]` keys.

overdue.description: Subjects past the interval. Zero on every state but `due`.

detail.description: What was measured, whether or not an interval applies.

remedy.description: The command or act that discharges it — or, on an `undeclared` clock, the key that would set it. Null when there is nothing to do.

due.description: `due` only. Clocks past their interval. A consumer MUST NOT render this as a fault count.

undeclared.description: `due` only. Clocks this corpus declared no interval for, which therefore can never come due.

strict.description: `doctor` and `due`. Whether `--strict` was passed. It is the only thing that makes a due clock exit nonzero, and the only thing that makes a doctor warning do so.

corpus_empty.description: `graph-check` only. Neither instances nor class definitions — a fresh repository, not a failure.

nodes.description: An array in `corpus-index` (index rows), `graph` (nodes with their resolved edges) and `diff` (changed nodes); an integer in `status` (how many there are). Two shapes under one name, which the field-presence check cannot see and a validating consumer would have tripped over.

sources.description: `catalog-audit` only. One row per catalog entry. Each carries THREE citation counts and they mean different things: `nodes` is corpus instances linking to the entry — the number every gate reads, and what `catalog-uncited` means by "no corpus node draws on this source"; `elsewhere` is other files under .yidam/corpus/ that link to it, which is class definitions and README prose; `citations` is their sum, retained with exactly the meaning it had before the two were separated. A consumer deciding whether a claim rests on a source MUST read `nodes`, never `citations`. Each row also names WHICH nodes cite it (`cited_by`) and how the entry's own hand-written `used-by` list disagrees with them (`drift`), so a consumer navigating from a node to its sources never re-resolves the corpus's links to find out.

entry.description: File name of the entry within .yidam/catalog/.

type.description: The entry's declared `type:`, or an em dash when it declares none.

obtained.description: Absent in the entry means obtained; only an explicit `false` claims otherwise.

citations.description: `nodes` + `elsewhere`. Kept so a consumer written against the single-count contract still reads the number it always read.

nodes.description: Corpus instances linking to this entry. The gate-bearing count.

elsewhere.description: Non-instance corpus files linking to this entry — class definitions and READMEs. Never added to `nodes`: a claim resting on a source and a page linking to one are different things.

cited_by.description: Repo-relative paths of the corpus instances linking to this entry, sorted. Exactly `nodes` of them — the count is this list's length, so the two cannot come to disagree. Instances only: a class definition or a README linking here is counted in `elsewhere` and not named, because it is not a node and has no row in a corpus view to sit under.

used_by.description: The entry's declared `used-by` list, verbatim and unresolved. Empty when it declares none. Hand-maintained and therefore able to drift from the citations, which are authoritative.

drift.description: How `used_by` disagrees with `cited_by`, compared by basename — or null when the entry declares no list, since absent is not drift. An object with two empty arrays is the different answer: a list was declared and it holds. Computed by the same function `catalog-used-by-drift` gates on, so the report and the gate cannot disagree about what drift is. A consumer MUST NOT recompute it.

claimed_not_citing.description: Basenames the list claims, that no citing node carries.

citing_not_claimed.description: Basenames of nodes that cite this entry, that the list omits.

range.description: `diff` and `check-diff`. The git range reported on, unnormalised, so what was compared is what the report says. Usually exactly as the caller gave it; `check-diff` may be run with no range, and then this is the default it resolved to — the merge-base with the default branch — rather than a blank.

vocabulary.description: `check-diff` only. How many names the ontology declares — classes, properties and relationships together. All three, because a domain concept can arrive in the ontology as a property of something else or as the name of a relationship, and a check reading only class names would ask about a concept the corpus already models.

introduced.description: `check-diff` only. Type declarations the diff adds, after regions declared `excluded` in .yidam/authorship.yml are dropped. A name the diff also removes is not counted: a struct moved between files is not a new concept.

aligned.description: `check-diff` only. How many of `introduced` match a declared name, kebab-cased. A count and never a finding: one row per correctly implemented concept would be a permanently non-empty report, which is where a real finding gets lost.

findings.description: `check-diff` only. Types the diff introduces that the ontology does not name. Every one carries `severity` (`warn`, or `info` where the file sits in a declared `generated` or `imported` region) and `question` — phrased as a question deliberately, because matching is by name and cannot tell a gap in the ontology from a helper it has no reason to know about. A finding may also carry `nearest`, an object of `name` (a declared name sharing a root with this one) and `shared` (that root). It is a lead and never a verdict: two names sharing a four-character prefix is a fact about two strings, arrived at without a model, and the finding exists whether or not a candidate was found — so a consumer must not render `nearest` as a confidence, a score, or a proposed fix. This report never gates: a consumer must not read a non-empty array as a failure.

blessed.description: `lint --bless` only. No gate ran, so no `gate` block is emitted.

active_phases.description: `status` only. Bounded work (`rigpa/*`, `phase/*`) not yet an ancestor of the baseline. Counted every `ma/*` and `rigpa/*` ref, and no `phase/*` ref, until the namespaces were typed.

settled_phases.description: `status` only. Bounded work already merged whose ref still exists; PHASES.md prescribes deleting these.

positions.description: `status` only. Standing `ma/*` elector positions, which are neither active work nor drift — divergence from the baseline is what a position is for.

state.description: `phases` only. What one inquiry ref currently is.

replay.description: `replay` only. Corpus health at each commit that touched the corpus, oldest first — the series every other report cannot give, because every other report answers about now. Always the whole series; `--every` samples the text rendering and never this.

commit.description: Short hash of the commit this row describes.

date.description: Commit date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. A date and not an age: an age is a function of when you ask.

nodes.description: Instance nodes present at this commit.

orphans.description: Nodes nothing points at, excluding classes the ontology says nothing should point at — the same population `orphan-in` reports.

by_class.description: Per class, keyed by class name. The corpus-wide figure is the one that misleads: it sums classes nothing is meant to point at with classes whose other instances are cited, and only the second is a finding.

catalog_expired.description: `status` only. Source records past the TTL this corpus declared, per entry or under `[catalog]`. Zero when no TTL is declared, which is every corpus that has not opted in.

meta_present.description: `index-status` only. Whether the index carries a readable `meta.json`. An index present but undescribable is a different state from an absent one, and the two used to render as the same sentence.

built_at.description: `index-status` only. Unix timestamp the index was built at, or null when there is no metadata. The raw stamp and not an age: an age is a function of when you ask, so humanizing it is the consumer's affordance.

built.description: `index-status` only. Civil date of `built_at`, so a reader need not convert one.

model.description: `index-status` only. Embedding model the index was built with.

node_count.description: `index-status` only. Rows in the index at build time. Compare against `status.nodes` to see what the index does not carry.

stale_nodes.description: `index-status` only. Corpus files modified since the build. This is the freshness verdict — a consumer MUST NOT recompute it by comparing mtimes itself.

collective.description: `sangha` only. Whether this repository runs collective governance, keyed on registered electors rather than on the directory: the template ships `sangha/` with a placeholder table, so a directory test would report every derived repository as collective from its genesis commit.

electors.description: `sangha` only. Rows of `electors.md` whose branch cell names a `ma/*` ref — which is what PROTOCOL.md defines an elector as.

role.description: The Role cell verbatim, markdown and all — it is prose written for a reader.

kind.description: `agent`, `human`, or empty. RFC-0012 attestation. NOT REQUIRED, and neither is any other attestation field: a released CLI predates the columns and a registry written before them fills none of them in, so empty means the registry does not say.

model.description: What produced this seat's positions, for an agent elector. Recorded, never privileged — Article II governs weight and Article III governs record.

version.description: The model's version, where the model name does not carry it.

config.description: A hash of the agent's operative configuration, never the configuration itself.

key.description: The seat's SSH public key in `authorized_keys` form — the key, not a fingerprint. `yidam lint` generates the `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` from this column at verification time, so the registry is the trust root and a key it does not carry verifies nothing. Empty means the seat declares its commits unverifiable.

branch_present.description: Whether the branch exists, local or remote-tracking. A registered elector whose branch is gone is a state to report, not an error.

positions.description: `sangha` only. Files in `positions/`, attributed by the `<elector>-<question>` naming convention.

elector.description: The registered elector whose name prefixes the stem, or EMPTY when none does. Empty is the honest answer for a position filed under a name the table does not carry; a consumer must not guess a nearest match.

question.description: The rest of the stem — the `rigpa/<evolution>` a resolution would carry.

resolutions.description: `sangha` only. Files in `resolutions/`, with their frontmatter.

evolution.description: The `evolution:` field, falling back to the filename stem.

tips.description: The `ma/*` tips the record says it read, verbatim — `ma/<elector>@<short-hash>`.

branch_present.description: Whether `rigpa/<evolution>` still exists. False is routine: the branch is often deleted once the resolution lands on the baseline.

synthesized_by.description: The `synthesized-by:` seats — the elector branch that executed the synthesis, and a list where it was joint. NOT REQUIRED, deliberately: a released CLI predates the field and emits records without it, and every record written before the field existed carries none, so a consumer that assumes it is present is wrong in two directions at once. Empty means the record does not say who executed it, which is a finding (`resolution-executor-unrecorded`) rather than a gap in this report.

source.description: `vocabulary` only. Repository-relative path of the GRAPH.md the **When** prose came from — the vendored copy if present, otherwise `yidam/prelude/`. Empty when neither exists, which costs the prose and nothing else.

verbs.description: `vocabulary` only. The closed commit vocabulary. MEMBERSHIP AND KIND COME FROM THE PARITY-CERTIFIED LISTS, not from GRAPH.md — a consumer that decided either from the document would be a second implementation of the predicate `lint --commits` gates on, and could green-light a verb CI then reports. GRAPH.md supplies `when` and nothing else.

when.description: The **When** cell, or empty when no GRAPH.md was found.

drift.description: `vocabulary` only. Disagreements between GRAPH.md's tables and the certified lists. Empty is the expected state; non-empty means the document and the predicate that gates on it have come apart, and the document is the half that is wrong. Three SDKs carry a comment saying the constants are 'kept in sync with prelude/GRAPH.md' and nothing verified it until this field existed.

subject.description: `vocabulary --check` only. One subject line checked the way `lint --commits` checks a committed one — but before the commit exists. Absent when `--check` was not given.

text.description: The first line, trimmed. Only the subject is checked.

verb.description: Everything before the first `: `, exactly as `classify_commit` reads it. Empty when there is no such separator.

kind.description: What the commit would be filed as. Total: every subject gets a kind, including one whose verb is unrecognized — which is precisely how a scoped operational verb ends up filed as Epistemic.

rule.description: `scope-suffix` is separate from `unrecognized-verb` deliberately: it has a known cause and a known double cost, and saying so is the difference between a squiggle that teaches and one that scolds.

severity.description: Read from the `unrecognized-verb` lint check rather than restated — all three rules are sub-cases of it. A consumer MUST render at this severity and not escalate: a squiggle stricter than the gate is an editor asserting a verdict nobody agreed to.

corpus_dir.description: `corpus-index`, `graph`, `neighbors` and `rename`. Repository-relative corpus root; every `node` path in the same report is relative to it. Emitted so a consumer never hardcodes `.yidam/corpus` — the one path in this contract a repository could plausibly move.

classes.description: `graph` only. The `.ont.yml` class definitions: what each kind of node is, the properties it may carry, and the relationships it may enter into. Exposed so a client offering completion reads the ontology from the CLI rather than becoming a second reader of a shape the prelude defines.

class.description: The `class:` field, falling back to the filename — `<class>.ont.yml` is what `graph-check` matches an instance's directory against, so the filename is the name that actually governs.

target.description: A CLASS NAME, not a path. `holds` on `person` targets `tenure`, and the instances it may point at are the ones in `tenure/`.

direction.description: `out` when instances of this class author the link, `in` when the other side does. A class declares both so its neighbourhood is readable from one file.

class.description: `neighbors` only. The class of the node asked about.

label.description: `neighbors` only. The label of the node asked about.

description.description: `neighbors` only. The description of the node asked about, so a client rendering a neighbourhood need not fetch the centre separately.

node.description: `neighbors` only. The node asked about, corpus-relative, or EMPTY when the id matched nothing. An unknown node is an empty report rather than an error: a client asking about the file you happen to have open must not have to know in advance whether it is a corpus node.

depth.description: `neighbors` only. The maximum hop count the traversal was allowed — not a per-neighbour distance; see `neighbors[].hops`.

neighbors.description: `neighbors` only. Breadth-first over the UNDIRECTED view of the graph: each reached node once, at its shortest hop distance, carrying the direction of the edge it was reached by. This is the same traversal `serve --mcp`'s `neighbors` tool performs, from the same function — half the interesting connections are inbound, which is why `orphan-in` exists at all.

direction.description: Relative to the node it was reached FROM, which at hops > 1 is not the node asked about.

hops.description: Distance from the start. Named `hops` and not `depth` because `depth` on this report is the maximum that was asked for, and a field meaning two things in one document is how a consumer reads one as the other. (`serve --mcp` calls it `depth` in its own output; that contract is unchanged.)

is_node.description: False for an `.ont.yml` target or a broken edge — reached, and not a corpus node. Reported rather than dropped: a neighbourhood that hid them would disagree with the graph it came from.

to.description: `rename` only. Corpus-relative destination; may name a different class.

applied.description: `rename` only. Whether anything was written. False for `--dry-run`, and false whenever `blocked` is non-empty. A client rendering a preview MUST check this before claiming the rename happened.

moves.description: `rename` only. The file move — one entry, or none when blocked.

line.description: 1-based. Zero on a `moves` entry, which is about a file rather than a line in one.

edits.description: `rename` only. Every `target:` rewrite, located. Covers inbound edges AND the moved node's own outgoing links, which need re-relativizing when it changes class — a same-directory target survives a rename inside one class and breaks the moment the node leaves it.

line.description: 1-based. Zero on a `moves` entry, which is about a file rather than a line in one.

unhandled.description: `rename` only. Markdown references to the old path. Reported, NEVER rewritten: RFC-0014 scopes the rewrite to the corpus walk, and the difference between 'renamed' and 'renamed and quietly broke the README' is whether anybody was told.

blocked.description: `rename` only. Why this cannot proceed. Non-empty means NOTHING was touched and the process exits nonzero.

commit_subject.description: `rename` only. A suggested subject in the closed commit vocabulary. `migrate:` and not `rename:` — RFC-0014's own example uses a verb that is in no list, which `lint --commits` reports and which makes `classify_commit` file an operational commit as Epistemic.

stale.description: `regen --check` only. REGEN blocks whose committed content is not what their generator produces. Empty when `passed`. Computed by running the same generator list `yidam regen` runs — a check walking its own list would be the third list that command exists to have prevented.

file.description: Repository-relative path of the file holding the block.

verdict.description: `index-verify` only. `match` — same vector space. `known-delta` — a DIFFERENT space, within a bound that runtime declared in advance; passes, and is meant to be surfaced rather than swallowed. `mismatch` — beyond every bound, or the wrong shape; degrade to keyword search. `unverifiable` — the index carries no witness, which is every index built before the field existed and is not the consumer's fault.

probe.description: `index-verify` only. The sentence the witness was taken on. Absent when the index carries no witness.

max_drift.description: `index-verify` only. Largest per-element difference between the provider's embedding and the witness. Absent when nothing was compared — a wrong dimensionality is not drift.

tolerance.description: `index-verify` only. The bound applied, which is the runtime's `known_delta` when one was granted.

runtime.description: `index-verify` only. The runtime a `known-delta` verdict was granted to. A consumer that does not name itself is held to the strict tolerance — inferring a bound would make the declaration a discount.

problems.description: `index-verify` only. What is wrong, and what to do about it.

filter.description: `log` only. Which filter produced this view.

total.description: `log` only. Commits in the range BEFORE filtering — a filtered view still reports what it hid.

epistemic.description: `log` only. Epistemic commits in the range, before filtering.

operational.description: `log` only. Operational commits in the range, before filtering.

entries.description: `log` only. The commits the filter admitted.

kind.description: From the parity-certified `classify_commit`. Operational verbs are the explicitly marked case; every other verb is epistemic, a totality the Dafny spec proves.

verb.description: Leading verb, or empty when the subject carries none.
